intro: Lesson 111: Plant responses: tropisms and auxin. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Set up cress seedlings in a shoebox with a side hole (adult cuts). Predict, then record growth over 3 days. Answer the exam-style question: explain your result.
questions.a: Seedlings bend towards the hole (1); auxin moves to the shaded side (1); shaded cells elongate more (1); more light for photosynthesis (1)
questions.model: Teacher shows a prepared box on camera with seedlings bent towards the hole.

questions.q: Seedling A tip covered with foil, B tip removed, C uncovered; all lit from one side. Predict and explain.
questions.a: A grows straight (tip cannot detect light) (1); B no growth/no bending (no auxin) (1); C bends towards light (1)

questions.q: Why do roots growing down help a plant?
questions.a: Anchorage and reaching water and mineral ions.

questions.q: Explain why a shoot grows towards light.
questions.a: Auxin made in the tip (1) moves to the shaded side (1); cells there elongate more, so the shoot bends towards light (1)
questions.model: Start at the tip: auxin made. Light from one side: auxin moves to the shade. More auxin, more elongation on that side. Uneven growth bends it to the light.

questions.q: Is a root growing downwards positive or negative geotropism?
